articles.title: Upcoming Programs and Event Reports
articles.summary: The article announces an upcoming talk by Dr. Sandra Faber on the future of Lick Observatory, with SJAA matching donations to save it. It also details the annual SJAA Yosemite Star Party at Glacier Point and includes two observing reports from Hunting Hollow and Coyote Lake Dam, highlighting galaxy viewing and challenges encountered.

articles.title: April Reports and Science Feature
articles.summary: This article covers a presentation for amateur astronomers on observing asteroid occultations, explains the turquoise fringe phenomenon during lunar eclipses, and announces the discovery of Kepler-186f, the first Earth-sized exoplanet found in a habitable zone. Additionally, it details an update to the NASA Visualization Explorer app for iOS devices, making NASA's scientific data visualizations more widely accessible. The content spans practical observing techniques, new astronomical discoveries, and science communication efforts.

articles.title: Cupertino Earth Day & SJAA Solar Observing
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted a successful solar observing outreach event at Cupertino Earth Day on April 6, 2014. Volunteers used various telescopes, including H-Alpha and Schmidt Cassegrain, to show sunspots and solar flares to 200-300 attendees. The event highlighted the active sun and educated the public on safe solar viewing and dark sky protection.

articles.title: KID SPOT
articles.summary: The 'KID SPOT' article offers engaging astronomy content for children, featuring space-themed jokes and a quiz. It includes a 'Night Sky Challenge' for May 2014, detailing visible planets, and provides an extensive overview of the constellation Virgo, covering its location, notable stars like Spica, associated celestial mechanics, exoplanets, galaxy clusters, and mythological connections. Quiz answers and a photo credit for a lunar eclipse are also included.

articles.title: Club Updates
articles.summary: This article from the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides comprehensive updates on its various programs, including successful school star parties and the Astro Imaging Special Interest Group. It announces numerous upcoming events like Astronomy Day, the Yosemite star party, and the Golden State Star Party, alongside a recap of a well-attended lunar eclipse viewing. The report also covers recent board decisions and schedules for dark sky events in May and June 2014.
